title: Concurrent prefetch sharded timebox for relevance scorer
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Reduce P95/P99 latency for the /rerank endpoint for medium-to-high QPS workloads while preserving or improving relevance quality. Deliver an adaptive concurrent prefetch + sharded microbatch timebox that enforces per-request token budgets and graceful fallbacks when time budgets are exhausted. Avoid single-threaded scorer bottlenecks and limit KV cache thrash during bursts.

Motivation: Current rerank tail latency spikes under bursty traffic and long-candidate lists. We need a solution that parallelizes scorer work across CPU/GPU lanes, bounds per-request token work with a sliding timebox, and coordinates KV prefetch to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

Scope:
- Implement sharded candidate partitioning so candidate scoring can run in parallel microbatches.
- Add adaptive token-budget enforcement per request (token ceiling + soft quota recycling) with a sliding timebox (soft deadline) per request.
- Coordinate KV prefetch across shards: cooperative dedupe + backpressure token budget signaling.
- Implement graceful quality fallbacks: early-exit heuristics, sparse-model short-circuit, or reranker approximation when timebox hits threshold.
- Expose metrics and tracing: per-request token_consumed, timebox_start/expire, kv_prefetch_hits/misses, shard_latency, fallback_triggered.
- Safety: ensure deterministic tie-breaking for ordering, avoid degraded quality for enterprise customers during rollouts.

Acceptance criteria:
- P95 latency for 95th-percentile customers reduces by >=20% on our internal replay workload with similar QPS and candidate length distribution.
- P99 latency shows measurable reduction and has fewer >2s spikes in stress tests.
- End-to-end relevance (NDCG@10) change within +/-1% for canonical prompt set, and documented fallback quality delta.
- Integration tests for KV-prefetch dedupe and shard backpressure.
- Gradual rollout plan with canary and automatic rollback if quality regressions >1.5% detected.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Parallelizing scoring increases contention for KV and CPU resources; we will limit concurrency by token budget and implement retry/backoff rather than unbounded queueing.
- Timebox is soft by default: first signal triggers optimistic early-promote of highest-scoring candidates; on strict SLO mode we will enforce hard truncate.
- Quality vs latency: provide knobbed policy per workspace (latency-first, balanced, quality-first). Default will be balanced.
- Prefetch dedupe complexity: we will implement an in-flight request registry with per-candidate dedupe keys and a small LRU short-term window to trade memory for lower duplicate work.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype sharded microbatch runner in dev environment that splits candidate lists across N shards and returns merged scores.
2) Add token-budget enforcement and soft timebox in runner; instrument metrics.
3) Implement KV prefetch coordinator: request-level dedupe + backpressure signals to prefetch workers.
4) Build fallback short-circuit path (lightweight sparse reranker model) and tie it to timebox expiry.
5) Load test across core replay workloads, iterate on shard sizing and token ceilings.
6) Canary rollout to 10% of traffic with close monitoring of NDCG and latency.

Rollout plan: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions.

Related artifacts: PRD: https://docs.internal.redwood/reports/rerank-sharded-timebox-prd, Design doc: https://docs.internal.redwood/designs/rerank-microshard-timebox, Perf dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/rerank/54022-canary

Deliverables: code + unit tests, integration tests for KV prefetch, perf benchmarks, monitoring/dashboards, rollout runbook.
